newsitem.title: UK: Analysts raise BG dividend forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Analysts raise BG dividend forecasts.

text.p: Analysts raised their dividend forecasts for BG Plc after the gas company announced it would change its accounting principles following a new pricing regime for its transport arm TransCo.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, one of BG's brokers, raised its forecast for BG's 1997 dividend to 8.5 pence per share from an earlier estimate of five pence, an analyst at the broker said.
BG earlier said it saw a 250 to 300 million profit boost coming from a switch to historic cost accounting, raising the prospect of a milder pay-out cut than earlier anticipated.
This more than offset initial market disappointment over the new pricing regime, analysts said.
The review calls for a one-off price cut which is slightly bigger than regulator Ofgas had originally called.
"Despite the fact they (BG) have lost most of the key issues, they have come out fighting with a more positive approach on the dividend," said one industry watcher.
BG remained tight-lipped, merely saying it would revise its dividend policy and announce the result in mid-September.
The group will switch to historic cost accounting after the Monopolies and Mergers Commission fixed TransCo's regulatory asset base at 11.6 billion stg.
This compares with a replacement cost of 17 billion in TransCo's books.
BG will write down five billion stg to bring its statutory asset base in line with the regulatory value.
The lower asset value means a lower depreciation charge, which in turns results in the profit boost.
Apart from this, analysts saw more upbeat results from the price review, pointing to gains made in revenue terms.
Under the agreed pricing regime, BG's total revenues over the next five years will be some 220 million stg higher now than proposed by Ofgas in August, BG said.
"That's a gain that was well worth fighting for," said Arthur Hepher, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
He believed BG's dividend might now turn out to be eight pence per share compared an earlier forecast of seven pence.
Hoare Govett, meanwhile, also upgraded its recommendation for BG shares to "undervalued" from "hold".
BG was 5-1/2 pence firmer at 218 pence in mid-afternoon business.

BG was called British Gas until it hived off its gas trading arm through a demerger in February. BG said at the time it expected a material fall in its 1997 dividend after a 14.5 pence pay-out last year.
